subject: Intermittent streaming elongation and response fragmentation — customer advisory
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@catalystai.com>, support@catalystai.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent streaming elongation and response fragmentation — customer advisory

Hi Alex / CatalystAI team,

We wanted to make you aware of an incident affecting a subset of hosted inference requests that use streaming (chunked) responses in eu-west-1. Beginning ~08:40 UTC this morning, some streaming responses experienced elongated gaps between chunks and, in rarer cases, truncated fragments which caused partial messages to be delivered to downstream systems. Our status page shows the incident here: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/STR-20280514.

What we know so far:
- Impact: ~3–6% of streaming requests in eu-west experienced long tail gaps (>2s between chunks) and occasional fragment drops. Non-streaming (full-response) requests were not affected.
- Root cause (initial): a latency inversion in the streaming mux that amplified rare KV-cache eviction spikes under a recently deployed routing change. Engineering has rolled back the routing change and added targeted throttling while we investigate.
- Mitigation in progress: rollback completed at 09:00 UTC; we applied a temporary throttling guard and increased KV cache retention windows. We’ve also enabled a fallback path that serves non-streamed full responses for high-priority customers while we validate stability.

Action for you:
- If you have production streams in eu-west, we recommend enabling the documented fallback (control-plane toggle) to receive full responses until we confirm normal chunk cadence. If you want us to flip it for you, reply and we’ll coordinate.
- We’ve attached a brief incident log and a status page snapshot.

Apologies for the disruption — we know streaming behavior is important for CatalystAI’s product workflows. I’ll follow up with a post-incident summary once engineering completes the investigation.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident update and link to postmortem — STR-20280514

Hi Alex — following up with the post-incident summary and remediation plan. Thanks again for your patience.

Summary (what happened):
- On 2028-05-14 08:40 UTC a routing change introduced a rare path that increased KV cache evictions under a specific request shape. The combination allowed the streaming mux to re-request state more frequently, which created jitter between chunks and in rare cases led to fragment drops.

Remediation completed:
- Reverted the routing change and rolled a guarded patch to prevent the special-case path from entering production.
- Increased KV cache retention windows and added backpressure throttles in the streaming mux.
- Added a streaming health signal and automatic fallback that will switch to full-response mode for requests that hit chunk-gap thresholds.

Impact and customer guidance:
- Impact confined to eu-west streaming requests; we estimate 3–6% of streams affected during the window 08:40–09:00 UTC on 2028-05-14. CatalystAI: we confirmed the fallback toggle for your org key (CATALYST-A).

Follow-up items (owners):
- INF-1127: tail-latency regression test and verification (owner: Ben Carter)
- INF-1130: improve streaming observability + parseable fragment markers (owner: Grace O'Connor)
- SEC-2201: audit the routing gating process to prevent similar deploys (owner: Security Eng)

Postmortem link: https://docs.internal.redwood.ai/postmortems/STR-20280514
Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/STR-20280514 (marked resolved)

If you’d like a short runbook call to walk through the fallback toggle and what indicators to watch on your side, let me know times that work and we’ll schedule.

Apologies again for the disruption — we recognize the downstream consequences for streaming-heavy integrations and made the fallback conservative by default while we complete the observable improvements.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
